tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the higher Mythos 5 tier in mid-June, billing the Mythos-class model as made safe for general use, though launch coverage immediately flagged controversial usage terms. Anthropic followed up with access details for the two tiers. Then on Jun 13 the story turned: a US government directive suspended access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and industry coverage reframed the launch as a release the models were deemed too dangerous to ship.
whats_new: The thread has flipped from a product launch into an access-and-policy story: a US government directive ordered Fable 5 and Mythos 5 suspended, and the follow-up coverage cast the models as officially too dangerous to release.
why_it_matters: For anyone building on frontier models, this is a live supply-risk lesson: a top-tier model can go from general-availability launch to government-ordered suspension within days. Keep a fallback model wired in rather than hard-coding a single flagship tier into production.
